title: Laptop AI Assistant: Safer Computer Automation with Strands Decider 2B
description: A laptop management assistant using AI-powered guardrails and Strands Decider 2B for safe file and application control.
body:
Laptop AI Assistant: Safer Computer Automation with Strands Decider 2B

Problem
Modern laptops need convenient automation without risking data loss. Users want natural language control ("delete old files") but current AI is either too slow (confirming everything) or too risky (acting without checks).

Solution
The Laptop AI Assistant uses Strands Decider 2B to evaluate destructive operations fast and safely. It instantly executes safe queries (file lists, app info) and carefully evaluates destructive actions (delete, move, terminate, launch) using three guardrail questions with calibrated confidence.

Architecture
Three layers: Conversation (Amazon Bedrock LLM) -> Safety (Strands Decider 2B) -> Execution (filesystem/process APIs).

Guardrail Pattern
For destructive operations, ask: (1) Are arguments grounded in user input or tool results? (2) Is this an explicit instruction or a question? (3) Should we confirm first?

Decision Logic: Proceed if confident and all checks pass. Request confirmation if low-confidence. Deny and guide if arguments fail checks.

Tools
Safe: enumerate_directory, get_file_info, list_processes, get_process_info
Destructive: delete_file, move_file, terminate_process, launch_application

Safety Features: Path validation blocks traversal attacks. System-critical blocklist prevents terminating kernel/system processes. Graceful 3-second timeout before force-kill. Permission error handling.

Evaluation
25 test cases (12 tune, 13 held-out test) covering explicit requests, ambiguous intent, grounded vs invented arguments, questions vs instructions.

Results: Design targets: <100ms safe operations, 1-2s destructive operations. Measured results pending ./kit bench.

Deployment
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime with Amazon Bedrock (conversation) and Strands Decider 2B (decision).

Why Strands Decider?
Fast (single forward pass), cheap (vs repeated LLM calls), calibrated confidence scores, deterministic, supports private/local deployment.

Built with the AWS User Group Madurai Strands Decider hackathon kit.
